the kidney of whole-body sublethal x-ray irradiated rats shows increased HU uptake, which is associated with a decrease in the tubular autoradiography, and these changes are reversed within two weeks.

the early circulatory disturbances in irradiated kidneys, as evidenced by the increased HU uptake, are accompanied by an early tubular dystrophic change, as evidenced by a decreased tubular autoradiography, which are both reversible within 2 weeks.
the early postirradiation renal changes in the rat include increased HU, decreased tubular autoradiography and decreased renal histologic changes.

the study of the renal function and structure of rats exposed to whole-body sublethal doses of X-ray radiation.
the early circulatory changes and their relation to the renal autoradiographic findings in the postirradiation period.
the study of the early circulatory changes and the subsequent postiradiation restoring renal process in the rat kidney after 800 R of whole-body irradiation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the early circulatory changes in the kidney are associated with a decrease in HU and a simultaneous increase in the renal autoradiographic granularity.
the early circulatory changes in the kidney, as a result of the whole-body irradiation, were accompanied with the early tubular dystrophy and the later tubular regeneration.
the early circulatory changes in the kidney after irradiation are associated with the early renal functional impairment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early circulatory, dystrophic, and postirradiation renal changes in the sublethally irradiated rat may be studied by the use of HU as a tracer.
the early changes in the kidney after whole-body irradiation are due to the circulatory disturbances, while the later changes are caused by the direct effect of radiation on the kidney.
the early post-irradiation kidney changes are not a result of the direct effect of the ionizing radiation on the renal cells, but are a part of a systemic reaction to the irradiation.
